Guides to the area

Capellades: the paper mill museum, La Bassa and the Abric Romaní

Capellades is 20 minutes from La Casa Vella. The Molí Paperer museum still makes paper by hand in an 18th-century mill (€7.50, booking needed), and next to it are La Bassa and the Neanderthal sites of the Abric Romaní.

Updated 2 November 2026

Capellades is 20 minutes by car from the house. It fits in a morning: the paper museum and, at weekends, the Neanderthal sites.

The Molí Paperer museum

It is in the Molí de la Vila, an 18th-century paper mill, and it is a working museum: paper is still made by hand there, and in the workshops you can make a sheet yourself.

  • Opening hours: Monday to Friday 10 am to 2 pm; Saturdays, Sundays and holidays 10.30 am to 2.30 pm. Booking is always required, on +34 93 801 28 50.
  • Guided visits at weekends and on holidays at 11 am and 12.30 pm, in Catalan; other languages if you book ahead.
  • Tickets: €7.50, reduced €4.25 (ages 8 to 18, retired people, students and the unemployed), guided visit included. The family workshop is €3.50 extra.
  • Closed on 24, 25, 26, 30 and 31 December and 1 and 6 January.

La Bassa

Next to the museum, La Bassa is one of the natural springs of the Carme-Capellades aquifer. Since the Middle Ages its water has driven flour, fulling and paper mills: it was channelled to the Costa mills, and the Molí de la Vila is the first of them.

The Abric Romaní and the NEAN

The NEAN, the prehistoric park of Capellades, brings together some twenty sites on the Capelló cliff, including the Abric Romaní, where Neanderthals lived. A visit includes an exhibition, an audiovisual, a guided tour of the site, spear-thrower and archery demonstrations and, if you like, a walk along the cliff.

According to its booking page, from September to May it opens on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays from 11 am to 2 pm, with visits at 11.15 am and 12.45 pm, and tickets cost €6 (€3 with a Molí Paperer ticket). The page gives no year, so check first on +34 621 123 715 or at reserves@neancapellades.cat.

A full morning

At weekends you can see the Molí Paperer at 11 am and the Abric Romaní at 12.45 pm, and be back in El Bedorc for lunch.
